transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Taylor Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Reddy (Redwood SE), Sandra Lopez (Willowcrest Security), Brian O'Neill (Willowcrest Platform Eng), Priya Malhotra (Willowcrest PM), Evan Kim (Willowcrest DevOps)

Summary:
Quick scoping to validate Willowcrest security gates for a 6-week pilot, define success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy), and agree on benchmark plan and timeline. Main asks: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC model, audit log granularity, KMS options, data residency and private deployment path. Redwood to provide SOC2 docs and benchmark runbook; Willowcrest to provide sample payloads and network constraints.

Topics: security controls, pilot acceptance criteria, benchmark metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, error rate), timeline, private deployment vs hosted options, KMS and audit logs, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and service account model.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Taylor Chen: "Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick check, can folks hear me okay?"
[00:05] Sandra Lopez: "Yep, can hear you. Sandra here, head of security for Willowcrest, joining from Boston."
[00:09] Brian O'Neill: "Brian here. Platform team. We'll be focused on network and deployment constraints."
[00:12] Taylor Chen: "Great. Maya from our infra team will walk through benchmark expectations and the security attachments Redwood supports. High level: we want to confirm SOC2/ISO posture and the operational acceptance criteria for the POC."
[00:23] Maya Reddy: "Hi all. I'll tee up the performance benchmarks then move into audit and access controls. Couple things up front — is the primary pilot using PHI? Sandra?"
[00:31] Priya Malhotra: "We will be sending de-identified but still sensitive clinical notes; some fields may be re-identifiable if combined, so we need strict data handling, ideally a private deployment or VPC option. We want to see logs and proof of encryption at rest and in transit."
[00:43] Sandra Lopez: "Yes. Our bar: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 baseline docs, SSO/SAML for user access, and RBAC that maps to our internal roles. Audit logs must include per-request metadata, request hash, model version, and token counts. Retention should be configurable — min 90 days for pilot but enterprise will be 7 years for certain records. Also KMS integration required — customer-managed keys preferred."
[01:03] Taylor Chen: "Understood. On SOC2 and ISO, we can share the attestations and our control mapping, and Maya will point at the specific audit trails we surface. For KMS, we support customer key wraps via KMS or HSM depending on private vs hostedconfigs — we'll include options in the security whitepaper."
[01:18] Evan Kim: "Quick network Q: do you require outbound internet egress? We prefer VPC peering or private link model due to our firewall rules."
[01:25] Maya Reddy: "We support VPC peering and private link for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we'll need approved egress and allowlist IPs; that said, for a pilot we can run a Dedicated pool in your region and do peering so no public egress is needed. There may be some telemetry back to our control plane — that's optional and can be toggled off for Private offers."
[01:43] Brian O'Neill: "Telemetry — are those logs or just heartbeat? Need to know what leaves the VPC."
[01:48] Maya Reddy: "Mostly anonymized telemetry for runtime health; audit logs and request payloads can be kept inside the customer network for Private deployment. We'll document exact fields and retention options."
[01:56] Priya Malhotra: "Let's talk acceptance criteria: we want POC to show stable 95th pct latency under 500ms for 512-token prompts at 5 RPS sustained, throughput of X tokens/sec — maybe you recommend targets? Also accuracy metrics — we have human-labeled golden responses."
[02:14] Maya Reddy: "For our suggested benchmark: p95 latency target 400-600ms for gen workloads at 512 tokens on a Dedicated 80-gpu cluster depending on model; for the pilot we can aim for p95 <= 600ms at 5 RPS and throughput goal of 40k tokens/sec aggregate. Error rate (timeouts/exceptions) under 0.5% across 24-hour run. We will run both cold and warm cache tests — cold start, then warm KV cache and batching enabled."
[02:41] Sandra Lopez: "We need the ability to reproduce runs. So canonical scripts + seed prompts, and a runbook that shows how to configure KV cache, batching, and quantization settings. Also show model variants — what's fallback behavior if capacity drops?"
[02:55] Taylor Chen: "We'll provide a reproducible runbook with scripts, and variant mapping. If the Dedicated pool saturates we can failover to a lower-cost variant with higher latency, or to a hosted slot — failover policy configurable. We'll document the impact on latency and token cost."
[03:10] Brian O'Neill: "For RBAC — how granular? Can we map to AD groups or SAML attributes? We need separation between dev, product, and security access. Also service accounts for automation."
[03:22] Maya Reddy: "Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for user provisioning; RBAC is role-based with custom roles available for enterprise. You can map SAML attributes to roles and we also support service account tokens scoped to specific models and routes. Audit logs record actor, action, target, model version, timestamp."
[03:40] Sandra Lopez: "Auditing must include request and response hashes and a pointer to where raw payload is stored (if stored). We may want to disable raw payload persistence for PHI. Can we redact or avoid storing full prompts?"
[03:53] Maya Reddy: "Yes, retention and redaction policies are configurable. We can store only metadata and response digests, or keep full payloads behind your KMS if that's preferred. For the pilot we'll propose metadata-only by default and enable full payload storage only if you opt in."
[04:09] Priya Malhotra: "Good. Timeline — we want to go from kickoff to acceptance in 6 weeks. Week 0: security review and benchmark plan. Week 1–2: infra prep and network peering. Week 3: benchmark runs and tuning. Week 4–5: evaluation and QA. Week 6: decision and potential expansion. Is that realistic?"
[04:30] Taylor Chen: "Yes, that's our typical 6-week pilot for customers with private requirements — we just need sample prompts and an approved network path ASAP to schedule the Dedicated pool. We'll aim to lock dates in the next 5 business days."
[04:41] Evan Kim: "One ops question: patching and kernel updates for the inference runtime — do you manage that? We need an upgrade window and a rollback plan so our service catalog stays stable."
[04:50] Maya Reddy: "We manage runtime and kernel-level updates for Dedicated and hosted. For Private/on-prem we provide an update lifecycle and optional air-gapped bundle. We can agree on maintenance windows during the POC and have a rollback snapshot for model runtime and container images."
[05:06] Sandra Lopez: "Encryption: must be AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit. KMS must support rotating keys on our schedule. Also want attestation of HSM if you use HSMs for key storage."
[05:17] Taylor Chen: "Yes — AES-256 and TLS 1.2+, we support KMS integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and in HSM-backed Private installs we can generate attestation docs. We'll include those details in the security packet."
[05:28] Priya Malhotra: "On model governance — we need model version pinning so we can track regressions to a specific model release and tie that into our evaluation dataset. Also a way to roll forward/rollback quickly if outputs degrade."
[05:38] Maya Reddy: "We have model version pinning and can do canary rollouts. Rollback is supported and we can tie evaulation alerts to a rollback trigger. We'll show a demo during the bench week."
[05:48] Brian O'Neill: "For benchmarks, can Redwood run a lab-style synthetic load from your side and simulate our latency profile, or do we need to run all tests from our VPC?"
[05:56] Maya Reddy: "We can run both. To validate network path and egress behavior it's best to run from your VPC. We'll provide the harness so you can run it; we can also mirror runs from our side to validate the control measurements. We'll sync on exact topology in the runbook."
[06:08] Taylor Chen: "Quick note on cost: pilot costs for Dedicated will be time-boxed — we'll give you an estimate in the pricing doc but pilots usually include a discounted reserved block for the pilot window. Post-pilot we can discuss commit levels if you want predictable unit economics."
[06:20] Sandra Lopez: "Final thing: compliance questionnaire. We'll need an NDA and an initial security questionnaire (SIG or CAIQ). Can you fill those?"
[06:27] Taylor Chen: "Yes, we'll send the NDA and a completed CAIQ + SOC2 docs. Maya will add the audit-log schema and runbook."
[06:34] Priya Malhotra: "OK, next steps recap?"
[06:37] Taylor Chen: "Recap: Redwood sends SOC2/ISO docs, security whitepaper, and the benchmark runbook. Willowcrest sends sample prompts/dataset and confirms network constraints. We'll aim to lock a bench week (w/c 2027-03-21) and reconvene after initial run to review metrics. Action items: see the items in the notes. Any objections?"
[06:55] Sandra Lopez: "No objections, just want the docs early so we can start legal and compliance review."
[06:59] Brian O'Neill: "We'll get Priya's dataset over by the due date and Evan will confirm firewall rules."
[07:05] Taylor Chen: "Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD with the NDA and SOC2 packet. Maya will share the runbook in a GitHub gist and a short demo recording. Bye all."

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: there are occasional mis-heard technical terms (K-V cache transcribed as 'K V cache', some model names anonymized), and some timestamps are approximate.

References (mentioned links):
- Redwood SOC2 + ISO packet (link provided in follow-up)
- Benchmark runbook + scripts (Maya to publish gist)
- NDA + CAIQ (Taylor to send)

Acceptance criteria (text from call, captured):
- p95 latency <= 600ms for 512-token generation at 5 RPS sustained for 24-hour warm run
- Aggregate throughput >= 40k tokens/sec during peak sustained intervals
- Error rate (timeouts/exceptions) < 0.5% over a 24-hour run
- Audit logs containing actor, action, model version, token counts, and request/response digests with configurable retention
- SSO via SAML + SCIM provisioning with RBAC mapped to AD groups; service accounts supported
- KMS integration with option for customer-managed keys and HSM attestation for Private installs
